Priya (PM): Quick triage — Customer Delta just sent a list of asks around tool/function calling. They want: schema validation, execution status in the result envelope, optional streaming, and a webhook async path. Can we scope an MVP for Q2? cc @Kevin @Nora @Ava

Kevin: Quick thought — streaming is high effort. Can we defer streaming to v1.1? For MVP I'd propose sync blocking + async webhook status (poll or callback). :thinking:

Nora: Agree on deferring streaming. For schema, we should avoid full JSON Schema for MVP (too flexible). Suggested constrained schema with primitives + arrays + objects + examples. Example snippet: ```json
{
  "name": "translate",
  "input_schema": {"text": "string"},
  "response_schema": {"translation": "string"}
}
```

Ava: If we expose webhooks, infra must enforce idempotency keys, 3 retries with exponential backoff, DLQ for failed deliveries, and header propagation for tracing (trace-id, span-id). Also need ACLs so customers can't poke internal endpoints.

Jordan (CS): Customer Delta said they'll pilot if we have a webhook + clear status codes in the result. Their timeline: end of next month — they can test only if SDK examples exist.

Priya (PM): Proposed MVP scope (draft):
- Must-have: request/response envelope with `status` (queued/running/succeeded/failed), `result` object, `error` object, `trace_id` header propagation.
- Nice-to-have for MVP: lightweight schema validation on platform for primitives + arrays, examples field, and an `execution_hint` (e.g., max_tokens_hint) to help runtime batching.
- Out: streaming, full JSON Schema, cross-tenant shared callbacks.

Acceptance criteria for launch:
1) API contract doc + example curl/SDK for sync and async flows
2) End-to-end canary with Customer Delta (successful run + fallback behavior)
3) Observability: per-call latency, status breakdown, error map in Console
4) Security review and infra retry strategy documented

Kevin: Rough engineering estimate: core runtime envelope + storage for async state ~2 sprints. SDK + examples ~1 sprint. Infra for webhook retries + DLQ ~1 sprint. If we do platform-side schema validation it'll add another sprint. So ~4-5 sprints total if we include validation. Without validation, ~3 sprints.

Nora: Also suggest we include an explicit `tool_version` and `schema_version` in the call metadata so we can roll forward/back. That helps canarying and automatic fallback to older tool variants.

Priya (PM): Decision for MVP: ship lightweight `tool_schema` (constrained types + examples) and require `tool_version`. Track schema validation errors in logs but do not block execution — fail open for now. Full JSON Schema support is an item for vNext. I'll own the RFC + contract doc. :white_check_mark:

eng-bot: Reminder: RFC review scheduled Wed 10:00. Invitees: @Kevin @Nora @Ava @Jordan (CS)

Kevin: I'll open a PR today with the example envelope and a proposed handler signature. Also will add an acceptance test: simulated 50 RPS with 95th/99th tail latency checks. :thumbsup:

Ava: We should add an infra acceptance: webhook delivery success rate >= 99% under nominal load, and DLQ alerts when >1% failure over 15m.

Priya (PM): Thanks all — I'll compile the contract + launch checklist and post it here before the RFC. If anyone has strong objections to the skip-list (streaming, full JSON Schema) speak up now.

Jordan (CS): No objections from Delta — they prefer earlier delivery with the limited schema. They can provide test prompts next week.

Kevin: Noted. I'll start carving up tasks and tag owners in the RFC.

Priya (PM): End.
